content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is it possible to connect to another controller using the UDP protocol? The other device is a proprietary black box that cannot be changed, but it provides access to IO through UDP. My objective is to use a [product_name] with a web-based HMI for monitoring signals from both the external controller and additional IO points. Keeping costs low is essential, so more advanced solutions like [product_name] are not an option. Any suggestions or alternative approaches would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!
The [product_name] relay does not suit this application. It would be better to consider an IIOT device. Certain third-party HMI systems may also be sufficient for your requirements.

The [product_name] [article_no] (standard [product_name] [version_no]) supports only Ethernet TCP/IP protocols, specifically S7 and, starting from [version_no], also Modbus TCP/IP. UDP and other communication protocols are not available.

analysis.insight_summary: Users aim to connect a [product_name] device to a non-modifiable controller using UDP for data visualization in a web HMI. However, [product_name] is limited to TCP/IP communications (S7 and Modbus protocols) and does not support UDP, restricting integration options with certain devices. This limitation affects low-cost solutions, excluding more advanced products like [product_name].
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for [product_name] to have UDP support for direct data exchange with an external controller and web HMI integration, with an emphasis on keeping costs low.
